sourcedFrom: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page (2024 — revision "Revision B 10.2.24" on the back page)
cleanIntro:
The LWRCI IC Mark II is an AR-15-pattern rifle built around LWRCI's short-stroke gas piston instead of direct gas: an operating rod, intermediate rod and piston cup under the M-LOK rail drive the carrier, so the carbon a direct-gas AR dumps into the receiver stays out at the gas block. It carries a 2-position gas regulator, Normal and Suppressed, reached through a hole in the rail.

The field strip is the familiar AR one — two takedown pins, buffer, bolt carrier group, charging handle — and needs no tools. LWRCI's routine maintenance follows every firing session; the detailed disassembly and maintenance (the bolt carrier group apart, the rail off and the piston system out) come every 2,000 rounds or weekly in the field, and need a Torx Plus IP20 wrench for the two rail screws. The piston parts run dry: LWRCI says never to oil them.

steps.title: Muzzle safe — magazine out
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction and keep it there. Press the magazine release and pull the magazine out of the well.
steps.prose: With a magazine still seated, working the charging handle only chambers the next round.
steps.quote: While pointing the muzzle in a safe direction, remove the magazine (if present) by depressing the magazine release and pulling the magazine out.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing the Firearm, printed p.17

steps.title: Hold the bolt catch down
steps.action: Press and hold the bottom half of either bolt catch lever. The IC's controls are ambidextrous, so the firing hand can hold the catch as well as the support hand.
steps.prose: Holding the lower half of the catch is what lets the carrier lock open when you draw it back.
steps.quote: Press and hold the bottom half of either bolt catch lever.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing the Firearm, printed p.17

steps.title: Charging handle all the way back
steps.action: With the other hand, grasp the charging handle, press its latch and pull the handle and carrier group firmly all the way to the rear. Any chambered round ejects; the carrier locks back on the bolt catch.
steps.prose: Short of the full stroke, the bolt catch can catch the front face of the carrier instead of the bolt.
steps.quote: grasp the charging handle, depress the latch(es) and firmly pull the charging handle and carrier group all the way to the rear.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing the Firearm, printed p.17

steps.title: Charging handle home
steps.action: Push the charging handle forward until it is closed and latched. The carrier stays locked to the rear.
steps.prose: A charging handle left unlatched can be knocked rearward and catch on things while you inspect.
steps.quote: Return the charging handle to the closed and latched position.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing the Firearm, printed p.17

steps.title: LOOK into the chamber
steps.action: Roll the rifle counter-clockwise until you can see the bolt and chamber through the ejection port. See an empty chamber and a bolt locked to the rear. In poor light, check by feel.
steps.prose: No case flying out is not proof of an empty chamber — the look is the check.
steps.caution: Do not depend on the fact that no casing was ejected on clearing.
steps.quote: Visually check to make sure that the chamber is clear and that the bolt is locked to the rear.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing the Firearm, printed p.17

steps.title: Clear it again before the pins
steps.action: Repeat the clearing check more than once before any pin moves.
steps.prose: LWRCI opens its field strip with this step because disassembly and cleaning are where negligent discharges happen.
steps.quote: Clear the rifle several times. Most negligent discharges occur during disassembly and cleaning operations.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Strip, printed p.25

steps.title: Rear takedown pin out to its stop
steps.action: From the left side, press in the rear takedown pin; from the right side, pull it to the right until it stops. It stays captive in the lower.
steps.prose: The pin stops on purpose — pulling past the stop is how detents go missing.
steps.quote: From the left-hand side, press in the rear takedown pin. From the right-hand side, pull the rear takedown pin to the right until it stops.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Strip, printed p.25

steps.title: Front pivot pin the same way
steps.action: Do the same with the front pivot pin: press it from the left, pull it right to its stop.
steps.prose: With both pins out the upper is free of the lower.
steps.quote: Repeat step 2 for the front pivot pin.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Strip, printed p.25

steps.title: Upper and lower apart
steps.action: Lift the upper receiver group off the lower receiver group.
steps.prose: Set the lower down with the hammer still cocked — the buffer retainer step needs it that way.
steps.quote: Separate the upper and lower receiver groups.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Strip, printed p.25

steps.title: Buffer retainer down — buffer springs out
steps.action: With the hammer cocked, press the buffer retainer down with a screwdriver, punch or similar tool. The buffer springs free under its spring — keep a hand over the tube.
steps.prose: The hammer has to be cocked so it is out of the way of the buffer.
steps.quote: With the hammer cocked, depress the buffer retainer using a screwdriver, punch, or other suitable tool. The buffer should spring free.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Strip, printed p.26

steps.title: Buffer and spring out of the tube
steps.action: Pull the buffer and the buffer spring out of the buffer tube.
steps.prose: That completes the lower's field strip.
steps.quote: Pull on the buffer to remove the buffer and buffer spring from the lower receiver.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Strip, printed p.26

steps.title: Charging handle back three-quarters
steps.action: On the upper, pull the charging handle about three-quarters of the way to the rear. It brings the bolt carrier group back with it.
steps.prose: Three-quarters is enough to present the carrier at the back of the receiver without dropping the handle out of its track.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle to the rear about three-quarters of the way.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Strip, printed p.26

steps.title: Bolt carrier group out
steps.action: Slide the bolt carrier group out of the rear of the upper receiver.
steps.prose: Keep it in one piece for now; it comes apart in Deep Clean.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt carrier group from the upper receiver.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Strip, printed p.26

steps.title: Charging handle down through the cut-out
steps.action: Pull the charging handle fully to the rear, then move it downward so its wide end drops through the cut-out in the upper's guide track.
steps.prose: It only leaves at the cut-out — do not force it anywhere else in the track.
steps.quote: Remove the charging handle by moving it downward so the expanded end of the charging handle passes through the cut-out in the guide track of the upper receiver.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Strip, printed p.26

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: upper receiver, bolt carrier group, charging handle, lower receiver, buffer spring and buffer. DEEP CLEAN carries LWRCI's detailed disassembly — the stock, the bolt carrier group apart, and the M-LOK rail off with the piston system out.
steps.prose: LWRCI's own limit: nothing beyond its field strip and detailed disassembly outside the factory or a gunsmith's shop.
steps.quote: Please note that rifles should not be broken down beyond the field strip unless in a controlled environment, such as the factory or in a gunsmith’s shop.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Strip, printed p.25

deepSteps.title: Stock off the buffer tube
deepSteps.action: Pull the adjustment lever under the buttstock straight down to free the stock pin, and slide the stock off the end of the buffer tube.
deepSteps.prose: That is all of the lower's detailed disassembly.
deepSteps.quote: Pull the adjustment lever straight down to disengage the stock pin, and then slide the stock off of the end of the buffer tube.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retainer out — straight, no twist
deepSteps.action: Cup the bolt carrier group in one hand. With a punch or a cartridge tip, push the firing pin retainer out into your cupped hand. Push it straight; do not twist it.
deepSteps.prose: The retainer is small and the cupped hand is there to catch it.
deepSteps.quote: push out the firing pin retainer in to your cupped hand. Do not twist the retainer during removal.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out the back
deepSteps.action: Slide the firing pin out of the rear of the carrier.
deepSteps.quote: Slide the firing pin out of the rear of the carrier.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Cam pin out
deepSteps.action: Lift the cam pin out of the bolt carrier group.
deepSteps.prose: The cam pin is the part LWRCI warns not to forget on reassembly.
deepSteps.quote: Lift the cam pin out of the bolt carrier group.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Bolt out the front
deepSteps.action: Draw the bolt out of the front of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt carrier group is now fully apart.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the bolt from the front of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Two rail screws out — Torx Plus IP20
deepSteps.action: With a Torx Plus IP20 wrench, take out the rail screws — one on each side of the rail. Set the screws and their washers aside where they cannot roll away.
deepSteps.prose: They go back in at the factory figure of 28 in-lbs, so note it now.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the rail screws with Torx Plus IP20 wrench. There is one screw on each side of the rail. Screws are installed at 28 in-lbs. Set the screws and washers aside.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.29

deepSteps.title: Regulator to its middle position
deepSteps.action: Through the hole in the rail, set the gas regulator sleeve to the intermediate position, midway between the Suppressed and Normal settings.
deepSteps.prose: LWRCI keeps the intermediate position for this one job: it is used only when removing the rail, never for firing.
deepSteps.quote: Set the regulator sleeve in the intermediate position between the suppressed and normal settings.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.29

deepSteps.title: M-LOK rail off
deepSteps.action: Slide the M-LOK rail off the upper receiver assembly.
deepSteps.prose: The piston system sits under it.
deepSteps.quote: Slide the M-LOK rail off the upper receiver assembly.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.29

deepSteps.title: Keep the piston cup forward
deepSteps.action: From here on keep the piston cup fully forward — angle the upper downward or hold the cup in place with a hand.
deepSteps.prose: The rods only separate cleanly from a cup that stays put.
deepSteps.quote: Ensure that the piston cup stays fully forward during the rest of the process, either by angling the upper receiver assembly downward or by keeping the piston cup in place with a hand.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.29

deepSteps.title: Operating rod back against its spring
deepSteps.action: Grip the operating rod near where it meets the intermediate rod and pull it back, compressing its spring. The intermediate rod comes away from the piston cup.
deepSteps.prose: The spring is under load from here until the operating rod comes out.
deepSteps.quote: Grab the operating rod near where the operating rod mates with the intermediate rod and pull back, compressing the spring on the operating rod. The intermediate rod will separate from the piston cup.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.29

deepSteps.title: Intermediate rod out
deepSteps.action: Keeping the spring compressed, pull the intermediate rod free.
deepSteps.prose: Do not let the operating rod run forward yet.
deepSteps.quote: Maintain the compression of the spring and pull the intermediate rod free of the assembly.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.29

deepSteps.title: Piston cup off the gas block nozzle
deepSteps.action: Lift the piston cup off the nozzle on the gas block.
deepSteps.prose: The cup and nozzle carry the hardest carbon on the rifle.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the piston cup from the nozzle on the gas block.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.29

deepSteps.title: Ease the operating rod out — LWRCI's stopping point
deepSteps.action: Let the operating rod's spring relax under control, then lift the rod out of the upper. That ends LWRCI's detailed disassembly.
deepSteps.prose: Detailed disassembly is as far as the rifle comes apart without special tools; anything further belongs to the factory or a gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: Relax the compression of the operating rod and remove it from the upper receiver.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC Mark II Individual Carbine — Operator's Manual — Revision B 10.2.24 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.29

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Solvent-soaked patch on a cleaning rod, pushed from the chamber end to the muzzle; let the barrel sit for several minutes.
Bore brush on the rod: punch the bore several times to break the build-up free.
Dry patches through the bore until they come out clean.

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Wipe the bolt carrier with a cloth slightly dampened with solvent.
Scrub the bolt face with a nylon brush dipped in solvent.
Deep clean: scrub the bolt, extractor groove included, the carrier and the firing pin; pipe cleaner through the firing pin hole and the bolt's firing pin cavity.
Wipe the solvent off; moderate coat of lube on the carrier body and cam pin, along the runners and the rear bosses, and two drops in the cam pin slot.
Deep clean: moderate coat in the carrier cavity the bolt sits in.
Do not lubricate the bolt face.

cleaning.name: UPPER RECEIVER AND CHARGING HANDLE
tasks: Wipe the inside of the upper receiver and the charging handle with a solvent-damp cloth, then dry.
Coat of lube inside the upper receiver and on the outside of the charging handle's long, thin section.
Point lube on the charging handle latch.
In blowing sand or snow, leave the inside of the upper and the outside of the rifle dry.

cleaning.name: PISTON SYSTEM
tasks: Deep clean: scrub the piston cup, intermediate rod, operating rod and the gas block nozzle, inside and out, with a dry brass wire brush.
Wipe off the remaining carbon with a rag and solvent; repeat if the nozzle or cup is heavily fouled.
Dry the piston parts completely.
⛔ Never lubricate the piston system — it runs dry.
In sand or snow, take the rail off at routine maintenance and brush the piston components clear.
Blue-green copper staining on the rail round the gas block is cosmetic; copper solvent removes it.

cleaning.name: LOWER, BUFFER AND PINS
tasks: Wipe the buffer and buffer spring with a solvent-damp cloth; light coat of lube on the spring.
Point lube on the hammer pin and trigger pin.
Light lube on the takedown pins.

reassembly: Deep clean only: operating rod in first and compress its spring; piston cup onto the gas block nozzle second; intermediate rod last — into the operating rod first, then into the piston cup. Spin all three to check nothing binds.
⛔ Never assemble or fire the rifle without the intermediate rod and operating rod in place — LWRCI warns it can fire that way and cause severe injury.
Deep clean only: M-LOK rail back on over the piston system; both rail screws and washers back in with the Torx Plus IP20 wrench — LWRCI installs them at 28 in-lbs.
Deep clean only: regulator back to Normal or Suppressed for how you shoot — the intermediate position is for rail removal only.
Deep clean only: bolt into the front of the carrier, cam pin in, firing pin in from the rear, retainer pushed straight back in.
⛔ Do not forget the cam pin — it can chamber and fire without it, and that shot can destroy the rifle.
Charging handle into its track at the cut-out, bolt carrier group in behind it.
Buffer spring and buffer into the tube, pushed fully in past the buffer retainer so the retainer captures the buffer.
Stock back on the buffer tube if it came off.
Upper onto the lower; front pivot pin in, then the rear takedown pin.
Run the function check before loading.
fncheck: Clear the rifle first. Seat an empty magazine and tug it to be sure the catch holds it. Pull the charging handle back: the carrier must lock to the rear on the empty magazine, and the handle must not return on its own — push it home. Drop the magazine; the carrier stays back. Press the large upper paddle of either bolt release: the carrier slams forward into battery (never onto a chamber flag). On SAFE, pull the trigger — the hammer must not fall. On SEMI, pull it — the hammer drops with a loud click. Charge it again holding the trigger down, then release the trigger slowly: you should hear the disconnector click and the hammer must stay cocked. Then clear the rifle again.
